name: Cookies
location: Firefox: cookies.sqlite ; Chrome/Edge (newer): Network\Cookies ; Chrome/Edge (older, pre-network-isolation): Cookies
purpose: Site-set tokens that provide insight into what websites have been visited and, for authentication cookies, what activities might have taken place there.
normal_baseline: Cookies correspond to sites regularly visited by the user, with expiration/session lifetimes consistent with normal session behavior.
anomalies: A session/authentication cookie for a sensitive application present on a host that never independently authenticated, consistent with cookie theft/replay (pass-the-cookie)
Cookie last-accessed time occurring after the associated user's account was reported compromised or after the user's last known logon
Cookies for a domain with no corresponding History entry, suggesting the cookie was set via a background/tracking request rather than a direct visit
anti_forensic_notes: Clearing cookies through browser settings removes the underlying SQLite rows, but a stolen/exported session cookie used elsewhere (pass-the-cookie) leaves no trace in the victim's own cookie store, so local absence does not rule out prior capture and reuse.
interpretation: Cookies establish that a site was visited and, via their secure/httponly flags and expiration, how the site intended the cookie to be used (session-only vs. persistent, script-accessible vs. not) along with origin site and last-access time. Session/authentication cookies are the direct target of session-hijacking attacks. An adversary holding a valid, unexpired session cookie can access an account without ever touching the stored password.
